brief: GS TMT desk roundup, 11 Oct 2026. NDX closed higher a fourth straight week (6 of 7) but index calm masks dispersion underneath: software outperformed semis by ~800bps, and while investors expect steady Mag7/semis earnings beats, confidence those beats convert to near-term alpha is lower, leaving the bull case resting on compute demand outstripping supply to support 2027+ capex. Separately, UoM consumer sentiment sits near 20-year lows and GIR's indicator shows light equity positioning even as the index sits near highs. Cyclicals vs defensives just had their worst week since mid-August, the Russell 2000 fell a fifth straight week, and Analog Semis decoupled from its usual ISM relationship, which the desk frames as either opportunity or warning. TSM (reports Thursday) sits upbeat on sentiment despite its biggest 4-day pullback since late July; GIR models $85bn/$98bn 2027E/2028E capex and stable near-term margins with out-year upside from the N2 ramp. A Dell site visit found management rejecting an AI-infrastructure-commoditization narrative, citing supply (especially constrained memory) as the gating factor to growth and storage/operating leverage as the margin driver, with enterprise AI adoption still early and FY27 revenue estimates up ~100% in a year. Inference-economy software names (SNOW, CRWD, PANW, NET, PLTR) stay bid near highs even as semis stumble because investors see them as deployment-levered rather than capex-levered, raising the question of whether earnings growth supports current multiples into earnings season.
